references.text: The people give the same answer as here: 'All that the Lord has said, we will do.' This shows the people's pledge of obedience before entering into the covenant.
Moses reads the book of the covenant to the people, and they repeat their pledge of obedience: 'All that the Lord has said, we will do and be obedient to.'
The people ask Moses to hear all that the Lord will say, and they promise to do it. The same pattern with the people's pledge of obedience.
Israel confirms its covenant with the Lord and promises to keep his commands and statutes.
The people renew the covenant under Joshua and promise to serve the Lord and obey him.
The book of Hebrews refers to Moses proclaiming all the commands to the people and describes the making of the covenant at Sinai.
This is the immediate premise for the people's answer; it shows the process from God's word to the people's response.
A theological parallel showing that the principle of obedience from Mount Sinai also applies in the restoration of worship.
This verse shows God's response to the people's pledge of obedience and confirms the purpose of the covenant.
This verse illustrates the fulfillment of the people's promise to do all that the Lord has said.
